title: Design voice-to-contact mapping strategy (1:1 vs 1:many)
description:
User consideration: A contact may have multiple distinct voice signatures (different embeddings). Need to decide mapping strategy:

Option A: 1:many - Contact has list of voices (ordered by best match/frequency)
  - Pros: Handles voice variations naturally
  - Cons: Computation latency, wasted time checking multiple voices

Option B: 1:1 - Single voice per contact
  - Pros: Simple, fast lookup
  - Cons: May not handle voice variations well

Consider: Which voices to try first (most frequent? best match?)

Decision needed before contact association implementation.

title: Plan for scaling speaker matching beyond 1k speakers
description:
Current approach: In-memory cosine similarity checks (fine for < 1k speakers per user). Over time (years), may need faster approach.

Consider:
- SQLite vector extensions (vector0, sqlite-vss)
- Approximate nearest neighbor search
- External vector DB (Qdrant, Pinecone) if multi-user service
- Per-user speaker isolation (already planned)

Make note for future optimization, not blocking current implementation.

comments.author: jrstear
comments.text: Current approach: In-memory cosine similarity (fine for < 1k speakers). Future scaling considerations documented in history/REMAINING_CONSIDERATIONS.md section 6 (Performance & Indexing). This is a future optimization note, not blocking current implementation.

title: Implement voice clustering and pruning strategy
description:
User consideration: Voices table may grow large with mostly unused entries. Need clustering/pruning strategy:

Approach:
- Use cosine similarity to find tight clusters of similar voices
- Take centroid of each cluster (representative voice)
- Prune redundant/unused voices
- Prevent table bloat

Implementation considerations:
- Clustering algorithm (e.g., hierarchical clustering with cosine distance)
- When to run clustering (periodic? on-demand?)
- Threshold for "tight" clusters
- How to merge/prune while preserving segment references

Future optimization to keep voices table manageable.

title: Save speaker embeddings from diarization for cross-recording matching
description:
Per seed.md: 'It seems to me that once a speaker is associated with a contact, all recordings by them would be able to be labeled with their picture and/or name, via a database lookup (rather than having to go back through all the recordings and reprocessing them). But i'd think each speaker has a vector and we could somehow suggest most-likely 3 speakers for unknown recordings.'

Currently, diarization results only save speaker labels (SPEAKER_00, etc.) and segments. The pyannote DiarizeOutput object provides speaker_embeddings (vectors) that should be extracted and saved.

Requirements:
- Extract speaker_embeddings from DiarizeOutput in diarize.py
- Save embeddings alongside speaker labels in JSON results
- Each speaker should have a unique embedding vector
- These embeddings will be used to:
  1. Build a library of known/unknown speakers
  2. Match speakers across different recordings
  3. Suggest top 3 likely speakers for unknown recordings
  4. Associate speakers with contacts persistently
